title: Behavioral proxy validity in macaque neuroscience: Developmental competence and contextual interpretability
title_zh: 猕猴神经科学中的行为代理有效性：发展能力与情境可解释性
abstract: Behavioral measures are central to nonhuman primate neuroscience, but their use as proxies for cognitive, affective, or clinical constructs requires more than accurate detection. We argue that behavioral inference depends primarily on two often- underexamined prerequisites: developmental competence and contextual interpretability. Developmental competence requires that the animal has acquired the experience, repertoire, and physiological capacity to express the target behavior. Contextual interpretability requires that functional significance be evaluated within the animal's developmental, social, and experimental setting. Without these prerequisites, immaturity or restricted rearing may mimic dysfunction, and adaptive coping may be mislabeled as pathology. We illustrate how proxies fail through developmental immaturity, definitional ambiguity, multifunctionality, and circular validation, and synthesize these considerations into a three-stage operational framework-Define, Interpret, and Validate-for evaluating behavioral proxies. To assess how frequently these inferential gaps occur in current practice, we conducted a mini-review of depression-related behavioral proxies across 56 macaque studies. We found that rearing history was sufficiently reported in only 17.9% of studies; operational definitions were increasingly omitted (from 26.3% absent in 2010-2019-58.3% in 2020-2026); contextual interpretation was considered in only 26.8%; and independent validation preceded model assignment in only 3.6%. These findings highlight the need for better-supported proxies, requiring developmental conditions aligned with experimental aims, a reproducible inferential workflow, and integration of ethological expertise with neural and physiological validation. Behavioral proxies should be treated not as convenient readouts but as construct-linked hypotheses to be defined, interpreted, and validated.
abstract_zh: 行为测量是非人灵长类神经科学的核心，但将其用作认知、情感或临床构念的代理需要的不仅是准确检测。我们认为，行为推断主要依赖于两个常被忽视的前提：发展能力和情境可解释性。发展能力要求动物已获得表达目标行为所需的经验、行为库和生理能力。情境可解释性要求在动物的发展、社会和实验环境中评估功能意义。若缺乏这些前提，未成熟或受限的饲养可能伪装为功能障碍，适应性应对可能被误标为病理。我们通过发展不成熟、定义模糊、多功能性和循环验证等因素说明代理如何失效，并将这些考虑整合为三阶段操作框架——定义、解释与验证，用于评估行为代理。为评估当前实践中这些推断缺口的频率，我们对56项猕猴抑郁相关行为代理研究进行了小规模综述。结果显示，饲养史仅在17.9%的研究中得到充分报告；操作定义在2010-2019年间缺失率为26.3%，2020-2026年为58.3%；情境解释仅在26.8%的研究中被考虑；独立验证在模型分配前仅出现3.6%。这些发现强调需要更有支持的代理，要求发展条件与实验目标相符、可重复的推断工作流程，以及将动物行为学专业知识与神经与生理验证相结合。行为代理不应被视为便利的读数，而应作为与构念相关的假设，需要被定义、解释和验证。
